title: Indian universities slip in QS Asia rankings again: No IIT, IISc in top 50
syllabus: GS2 › Issues relating to development and management of education and human resources · GS3 › Science and technology: indigenisation and development of new technology (research capacity)
summary: No Indian university made the top 50 of the QS Asia Rankings 2027 for the second year; IIT Delhi fell to 66th, though India has 325 ranked institutions and leads Asia on papers per faculty.
ideas: Output without impact: India leads Asia in research output per faculty (27 universities in the top 50, five in the top 10), but has only three in Asia's top 50 for citations per paper.
GS2 · Higher education / GS3 · Research
Indian universities publish a lot but are cited little: the challenge is research quality, not quantity.

Expansion is not excellence: ranked Indian institutions rose from 24 in 2016 to 325, second only to China (448), yet 71% slipped this year and all six top-ranked fell; IIT Delhi dropped from 59th to 66th.
GS2 · Higher education
India's rise from 24 to 325 ranked institutions shows access expanding faster than quality.
A strong base: 15 Indian universities share first place in Asia for staff with PhDs, showing doctoral capacity is not the constraint.
GS2 · Human resources
With more PhD-qualified faculty than most of Asia, India's gap lies in research impact and international recognition.
Competition is rising: 195 new entrants across Asia; QS says India must translate research capacity into impact and international recognition.
GS2 · Education / global competitiveness
As Asian rivals improve faster, standing still in research quality means falling behind.
keywords: Citations per paper
A measure of how often published research is cited, a proxy for impact
GS2 · Higher education
Low citations per paper show that Indian research is visible in volume but not in influence.
Massification of higher education
Rapid expansion of enrolment and institutions
GS2 · Education
Massification without matching investment in faculty and research dilutes quality.
Internationalisation
Attracting foreign students and faculty and global collaboration
GS2 · Education
Weak internationalisation keeps Indian universities low on global reputation scores.
data: 325 ranked (China 448); only 3 in top 50 for citations
Indian institutions in QS Asia Rankings 2027; India's research impact
India has 325 institutions in the QS Asia Rankings 2027, second only to China, but only three in Asia's top 50 for citations per paper.
examples: India's top institution slips as Asian competition grows
Even India's best, IIT Delhi, slipped to 66th in Asia in 2026: a signal for research-led reform.
pyqs: Quality of higher education; would entry of foreign institutions help?
Scientific research in Indian universities is declining; critically examine.
Initiatives to propel research in premier institutes for gainful innovation.
Demographic dividend needs an educated, skilled and creative workforce.

trend.t: Higher education questions focused on quality and competitiveness (foreign institutions, 2015) and on research in universities and premier institutes (2014, 2015), linked to the demographic dividend (2016). Later education questions moved to school and policy (NEP 2020 in GS4) and examinations (2024).
trend.watch: Research quality in universities has not been asked directly since 2015, so it is a likely return area now that NEP 2020 and the ANRF are in place.
focus: Expansion vs quality in higher education
Higher education and the demographic dividend

potential: "Indian higher education has expanded in numbers but not in research impact." Examine the reasons and suggest reforms. (10 marks)

title: NTA overhaul: 5,000 experts empanelled for setting, vetting question papers
syllabus: GS2 › Issues relating to education; Statutory and executive bodies; Government policies · GS4 › Probity and integrity in public institutions
summary: After the NEET-UG paper leak, the NTA has empanelled thousands of vetted experts and is building a large question bank so papers can be finalised minutes before exams.
ideas: Crisis forced reform: after the NEET-UG paper leak in May, which led to protests and the Education Minister's resignation, the NTA dropped about 600 experts and moved its headquarters.
GS2 · Education governance
Exam leaks erode public trust, forcing institutional overhaul at testing bodies.
Vetting for integrity: experts are empanelled after multi-layer checks, including no links to coaching institutes, and must sign and reaffirm non-disclosure agreements.
GS2 · Institutional reform / GS4 · Integrity
Background checks and confidentiality rules guard against conflicts of interest in exam setting.
Design against leaks: a large question bank lets papers be finalised minutes before an exam, and setters do not know which exam a question is for.
GS2 · Exam reform
A large question bank and late paper assembly reduce the window for leaks.
Technology helps: most NTA exams except NEET are computer-based, and AI-translated material is reviewed by experts.
GS2 · E-governance
Computer-based testing and secure question banks make exams harder to compromise.
keywords: Question bank
Large pool of pre-vetted questions drawn at random
GS2 · Exam reform
A large question bank prevents setters from memorising papers.
Conflict of interest
Personal interest clashing with official duty
GS4 · Integrity
Barring experts linked to coaching institutes removes conflicts of interest.
Institutional credibility
Public trust in an institution's fairness
GS2 · Governance
Exam integrity is central to the credibility of testing institutions.
examples: Vetted experts, NDAs and a large question bank
GS2 · Education, institutional reform · GS4 · Probity, conflict of interest
The NTA's overhaul shows how an institution rebuilds trust after a breach through systems, not slogans.
pyqs: Aims of the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.
potential: Examine the measures needed to restore credibility to India's national entrance examinations. (10 marks)
